title: The danger of not recognising the Grace of God Part 3
scripture_text: “Meanwhile, the older son was in the field. When he came near the house, he heard music and dancing So he called one of the servants and asked him what was going on.‘Your brother has come,’ he replied, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has him back safe and sound.’ “The older brother became angry and refused to go in. So his father went out and pleaded with him. But he answered his father, ‘Look! All these years I’ve been slaving for you and never disobeyed your orders. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends. But when this son of yours who has squandered your property with prostitutes comes home, you kill the fattened calf for him!’ ‘My son,’ the father said, ‘you are always with me, and everything I have is yours. But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’’
devotional:
For the elder son, his relationship with his father was built on duty not love. He found no pleasure or joy in serving his father, he saw himself as dutiful servant not as a beloved son.

I believe that the most effective ploy of the evil one is to prevent Christians from thinking like sons/daughters of God. Once we stop believing that we are children of God, it won’t be long until there will be some distance between us and the Father.

Duty or a ‘must do’ attitude dries up a person’s relationship with the father. The idea behind the word duty is to owe something. If we base our relationship on the basis that we owe God something, and not on the basis of Grace, it will not be a healthy relationship. I could never give to God what I owe him, but that is okay. In fact it is better than okay; For God will only accept us on the basis of His grace alone. The elder sons’ relationship with the father was not based on Grace. He had an ‘I deserve,’ attitude, therefore, he was unable to understand grace, receive grace or be gracious.

Our father God wants our hearts not our duty, he wants our love more than he wants our service, he wants us to know and understand his heart.

The elder son related to his father with a ‘deal mentality.’ Let me explain, listen to what he says to his father ‘All these years I’ve been slaving for you, (which was a lie as we shall see.) and never disobeyed your orders. Yet you never even gave me a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.’ Do you see what he is saying here? He is saying ‘because I have been such an obedient son, you owe me. I have ticked all the boxes, and have done all my duties. I think I deserve something in return. He wasn’t really slaving for the Father, he was serving himself.

It is very easy for anyone of us to develop a ‘deal mentality’ when it comes to our relationship with God our Father. We may never verbalise these thoughts, but we can think things like. ‘I have been faithful, God has to bless me.’ Or, ‘If I am obedient then I deserve God to answer my prayers.’ We think, If I repent more, read the bible more, pray more, obey more, serve more and just try harder to be a good Christian, God will come through for me.’

This kind of thinking in Pharisaical, therefore it is contrary to the Kingdom of God and anti-grace. God will only deal with us on the basis of Grace, nothing we can do or say will ever make us more deserving of God’s love or blessing.

The elder son was unable to celebrate.

This celebration is the very essence of the Father’s heart; it expressed the longing and desire of his heart. This was what the father had longed and hoped for, for years. However, because of what was going on in the heart of the older brother, he was unable to celebrate, understand or appreciate the heart of his Father. This celebration underscored what was really important. It highlighted that love, mercy, grace, forgiveness, acceptance and relationships are extremely important. This celebration could be defined as divine satisfaction. This was the happiest day in the life of the Father, but his older son was emotionally detached.

This elder son must be one of the saddest people we meet in all of Scripture. As the Father and younger brother, along with their friends and neighbours enjoy the transforming and healing glory of grace, the elder son stands outside in the cold shadows nursing his anger. As the sound of music and dancing fills the air and the joyous noise of celebration surrounds him, he must have felt so lost, so detached, so far from home. We are not told if he ever went into the celebration, or if he remained trapped in his Pharisaical mindset having a blind spot to the glory and wonder of the grace of God.

God never wants us to feel left out in the shadows. His heart is for all of us to experience His grace. We do not need to try harder, earn more, do more or be better to receive His grace. He accepts and love us unconditionally when we put our trust in Him.

Let’s end by pointing out one more thing from the parable. We are told that the Father went out and pleaded with him. The word that is used is parakaleō which means to come along beside to encourage or comfort. This is amazing; the father had every right to be angry, his eldest son had publicly shamed him by refusing to join the celebration, but his father went out to him and shows him tender grace. Unfortunately the son still didn’t get it.

If any of us are like the elder brother, our father is pleading with us; he is gently saying ‘it does not have to be this way.’ In great tenderness he is saying, ‘it’s time to come home, let us celebrate together.’
prayer: Father may I know the glory of celebrating with you by receiving your grace.
